CARD CAPTIONS — NATURE (migrated 2026-08-30): Douro Valley Vineyards: Harvest runs into October, so the terraces are busy and gold | Cabo da Roca & the Sintra Coast: Twenty minutes from Sintra; windy even in warm weather | Sete Cidades Twin Lakes: Cloud usually clears by late morning — go from Vista do Rei | Furnas Valley: The stew comes out of the ground around noon; order a day ahead | Lagoa do Fogo: The access road shuts in fog — check before driving up

CARD CAPTIONS — CITIES (migrated 2026-08-30): Porto: Ribeira and the iron bridge are ten minutes apart on foot | Lisbon: Built on seven hills — the trams and street lifts exist for a reason | Sintra: Go at opening; the palaces queue badly from about 11am | Ponta Delgada: Nothing on the island is more than an hour away | Coimbra: An easy stop halfway along the Porto–Lisbon drive | Óbidos: Directly on the Douro–Sintra drive; an hour is enough

CARD CAPTIONS — FOOD (migrated 2026-08-30): Pastel de Nata: Pastéis de Belém in Lisbon has baked them since 1837 | Francesinha: Café Santiago on Rua de Passos Manuel, serving them since 1959 | Bifana: Conga on Rua do Bonjardim — about €2.50, with a queue at lunchtime | Cozido das Furnas: Buried at dawn, dug up around noon — order a day ahead | São Jorge Cheese: Sold in every island supermarket; the aged wheels are the sharp ones | Travesseiros de Sintra: Piriquita on Rua das Padarias — expect a queue out the door

CARD CAPTIONS — THINGS TO DO (migrated 2026-08-30): Terra Nostra Thermal Pool: Open until 22:00; Poça da Dona Beija nearby runs even later | Ponta da Ferraria: Go within two hours of low tide or it is simply cold sea | Gorreana Tea Plantation: Free entry and free tea; no booking, just turn up | Whale & Dolphin Boats: Half-day trips from Ponta Delgada — the one thing worth booking ahead | Tram 28 & LX Factory: Board at Martim Moniz for a seat; LX Factory is busiest on Sundays | The Douro Historic Train: Runs weekends into October; the regular line runs daily and is nearly as good
title: Porto to Lisbon, then Volcanic São Miguel: A Portugal & Azores Road Trip

heroImage.caption: Sete Cidades twin crater lakes, São Miguel, Azores

brief: Two and a half weeks that feel like two trips in one: charming riverside towns and hillside palaces across mainland Portugal, then a short flight to the Azores for green, volcanic scenery unlike anywhere else in Europe. Easy walking, pretty architecture, wonderful pastries, and views worth every photo.

facts.bestSeason: Late September–early October, warm on the mainland and mild and green in the Azores
facts.language: Portuguese; English widely spoken in tourist areas
facts.timezone: Western European Time (Azores is 1 hour behind mainland Portugal)
facts.driving: Right-hand traffic, good highways and scenic secondary roads
facts.flightsWithinTrip: One short flight partway through the trip, from Lisbon to Ponta Delgada

primary.heading: Mainland, then mid-Atlantic
primary.intro: Two trips in one. Riverside cities and hillside palaces first, then a short flight to a green volcanic island that looks nothing like the country you just left.

nature.heading: Terraced valleys and crater lakes
nature.intro: The mainland's landscape is cultivated — vineyards stacked in terraces down to the river. The Azores' is raw: craters, steam vents and hillsides greener than southern Europe has any right to be.

cities.heading: Tiled façades and hilltop old towns
cities.intro: Portuguese cities are built on hills and covered in patterned tile, which means viewpoints round every corner and something worth looking at on every wall.

food.heading: Custard tarts and pork sandwiches
food.intro: Eating here is cheap, savoury and done standing at a counter. The pastries alone would justify the flight.

why.heading: Why this one keeps coming back up
why.intro: Easy to travel, warm well into autumn, and it changes character completely halfway through without you having to work for it.

thingsToDo.heading: Hot springs, tea fields and old trams
thingsToDo.intro: Most of what there is to do here you can decide on the morning of — a thermal pool, a tram, a boat. Only the whale trip really wants booking ahead.

itinerary.description: Land in the evening, sleep by the airport, and start fresh in the morning.
Colourful riverside streets, the iron bridge, tiled churches, and a francesinha you will not finish.
Terraced vineyards folding down to the river, at harvest, with a historic train running the gorge.
Fairy-tale palaces in forested hills, Atlantic cliffs twenty minutes away, and pastries worth the queue.
Trams through Alfama, hilltop viewpoints, street art at LX Factory, and the best eating of the mainland.
A short flight to a completely different Portugal — green, volcanic and quiet.
Steaming ground, thermal pools you can sit in after dark, and a stew cooked in the earth.
Fly home with a full memory card.

primaryHighlights.title: Porto & the Douro Valley
primaryHighlights.description: Charming riverside streets in Porto, then a scenic drive through one of Europe's most beautiful vineyard valleys.
primaryHighlights.caption: Dom Luís I bridge over Porto

primaryHighlights.title: Lisbon & Sintra
primaryHighlights.description: Fairy-tale palaces and a hilly, colourful capital city, all within easy reach of each other.
primaryHighlights.caption: Pena Palace in Sintra

primaryHighlights.title: São Miguel, Azores
primaryHighlights.description: A short flight away, but a totally different world of crater lakes, hot springs and green hills.
primaryHighlights.caption: Misty lake at Sete Cidades

natureHighlights.title: Douro Valley Vineyards
natureHighlights.description: Rolling terraced vineyards along the river — one of the prettiest drives in Europe.
natureHighlights.caption: Terraced vineyards above the Douro

natureHighlights.title: Cabo da Roca & the Sintra Coast
natureHighlights.description: The westernmost point of mainland Europe — a lighthouse on a 140 m cliff, with empty surf beaches either side.
natureHighlights.caption: Sea stack at Cabo da Roca

natureHighlights.title: Sete Cidades Twin Lakes
natureHighlights.description: The classic viewpoint over two lakes, one blue and one green, sitting side by side inside a giant volcanic crater.
natureHighlights.caption: Twin lakes from Vista do Rei

natureHighlights.title: Furnas Valley
natureHighlights.description: Bubbling hot springs and steaming vents in a peaceful green valley.
natureHighlights.caption: Lagoa das Furnas from above

natureHighlights.title: Lagoa do Fogo
natureHighlights.description: A striking crater lake viewpoint, perfect for a short scenic walk.
natureHighlights.caption: Lagoa do Fogo crater lake

cityHighlights.title: Porto
cityHighlights.description: The colourful, stacked houses of Ribeira tumbling down to the riverfront — Porto's most photographed corner.
cityHighlights.caption: Ribeira district across the Douro

cityHighlights.title: Lisbon
cityHighlights.description: The Belém Tower, standing right at the water's edge — one of the city's most iconic landmarks.
cityHighlights.caption: Belém Tower at dusk

cityHighlights.title: Sintra
cityHighlights.description: The mysterious, moss-covered Quinta da Regaleira, with its hidden tunnels and spiral well.
cityHighlights.caption: Quinta da Regaleira palace

cityHighlights.title: Ponta Delgada
cityHighlights.description: A relaxed, pretty harbour town and the easygoing heart of the Azores.
cityHighlights.caption: Ponta Delgada town hall at dusk

cityHighlights.title: Coimbra
cityHighlights.description: A charming riverside university town, worth a stop if you have a few extra days.
cityHighlights.caption: Coimbra skyline from the Mondego

cityHighlights.title: Óbidos
cityHighlights.description: A whitewashed village entirely inside its medieval walls, which you can walk right around above the rooftops.
cityHighlights.caption: Óbidos rooftops and town walls

culinaryHighlights.title: Pastel de Nata
culinaryHighlights.description: Warm custard tarts, best enjoyed fresh from the oven — the trip's sweetest habit.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Custard tarts at Pastéis de Belém

culinaryHighlights.title: Francesinha
culinaryHighlights.description: Porto's indulgent meat-and-cheese sandwich, smothered in a rich sauce.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Francesinha with fried egg and sauce

culinaryHighlights.title: Bifana
culinaryHighlights.description: A simple, delicious pork sandwich found at cozy little spots everywhere.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Bifana sandwich with cheese and egg

culinaryHighlights.title: Cozido das Furnas
culinaryHighlights.description: A hearty stew cooked underground by the earth's own heat — a true Azores original.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Cozido das Furnas on the plate

culinaryHighlights.title: São Jorge Cheese
culinaryHighlights.description: A sharp, delicious Azorean cheese, great for picking up at a local market.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Wheel of São Jorge cheese

culinaryHighlights.title: Travesseiros de Sintra
culinaryHighlights.description: Warm almond-cream pastry pillows, made in the same Sintra bakery since 1862 and sold faster than they cool.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Travesseiro and queijada pastries

thingsToDo.title: Terra Nostra Thermal Pool
thingsToDo.description: A huge ochre-orange pool of warm iron-rich water in the middle of a botanical garden. Bring a dark swimsuit — the iron stains.
thingsToDo.caption: Swimmers in the ochre thermal pool

thingsToDo.title: Ponta da Ferraria
thingsToDo.description: Swim in the sea where a hot spring pours into a rock pool on the shoreline. The temperature depends entirely on the tide.
thingsToDo.caption: Rocky coastline at Ponta da Ferraria

thingsToDo.title: Gorreana Tea Plantation
thingsToDo.description: The only tea plantation in Europe, working since 1883. You walk in free, wander the machinery floor, and drink as much as you like.
thingsToDo.caption: Tea rows at Gorreana plantation

thingsToDo.title: Whale & Dolphin Boats
thingsToDo.description: Sperm whales and several dolphin species sit off São Miguel year-round, and the boats still run through October.
thingsToDo.caption: Dolphins off São Miguel

thingsToDo.title: Tram 28 & LX Factory
thingsToDo.description: Ride the old wooden tram up through Alfama, then spend an afternoon in a converted industrial yard full of street art and shops.
thingsToDo.caption: Lisbon tram in a narrow street

thingsToDo.title: The Douro Historic Train
thingsToDo.description: A steam-hauled train along the river gorge between Régua and Tua, on one of the prettiest rail lines in Europe.
thingsToDo.caption: Vintage train at a Douro station

otherPerks: Thermal pools you can sit in after dark, for about ten euros
Custard tarts still warm from the oven, more or less everywhere, for a euro
The sea is still swimmable in October on both the mainland and the islands
Trams and hillside lifts do Lisbon's climbing for you
Azulejo tilework and street art on ordinary buildings, not just the monuments
One of the cheapest countries in western Europe to eat and drive in
English almost everywhere, and motorways that are new and empty
Two hours of flying turns a city trip into an island one
